title: Nvidia demand continues to outweigh supply, JPMorgan says
text: Nvidia's supply chain remains under pressure as demand for its AI chips continues to surpass availability, JPMorgan said following an investor meeting with Toshiya Hari, the company's vice president of investor relations and strategic finance. Demand continues to outweigh supply, keeping lead times stretched but stable, JPMorgan noted. Nvidia reiterated that its upcoming Vera Rubin platform is on track for a second-half 2026 launch despite industry speculation of delays. Nvidia's FQ2 inventory increase, up 33% quarter-on-quarter to $8.7 billion, was in support of the Blackwell Ultra (BWU) ramp rather than a build-up of older GB200 chips. On China, Nvidia has received U.S. government approval to export its H20 GPUs, but no purchase orders have been booked. JPMorgan believes rack production will inflect higher in the second half of fiscal 2026, with supply chain partners boosting capacity.

title: Tesla Faces US Auto Safety Probe Over Risk of Suspension Failure
text: US auto safety regulators opened an investigation into Tesla Inc.'s most-popular models after a series of complaints by drivers over the sudden failure of suspension in their vehicles. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has received 156 reports of apparent suspension issues in Teslas, which potentially causes a loss of vehicle directional control, according to documents posted to the agency's website. The preliminary evaluation involves an estimated 1.2 million vehicles, including Model 3 sedans from the 2018 to 2020 model years and Model Y SUVs from 2021 to 2023.

title: Nvidia's Q3 2026 Earnings Preview: Supply Chain Challenges and AI Demand
text: Nvidia is set to announce its Q3 2026 earnings amidst robust AI chip demand and supply chain hurdles. These collaborations underscore Nvidia's dominance in the AI chip market, as enterprise demand for advanced AI solutions continues to surge. Analysts are closely watching how Nvidia navigates supply chain constraints, which could delay fulfillment of these massive orders. Nvidia's projected revenue for fiscal Q3 2026 stands at $55.2 billion. The supply chain challenges and increased competition could spur innovation in semiconductor manufacturing and AI applications.
